Yes please! The mouse behaviors in opencode drive me nuts because they're so idiosyncratic (vs. macOS behaviors). The end result is my brain gets trained to just avoid the mouse as much as possible to avoid constantly being surprised. A few examples:
1. I can't double-click to select words
1. I can't triple-click to select lines
1. When I single-click and drag, the selection goes away when I release the click (instead of staying selected)
1. When I single-click and drag, copy happens automatically when I release the click (instead of requiring cmd+c)
1. Scrolling moves with different speed and momentum than my terminal

Ideally opencode/opentui could add support for all of these behaviors, and also implement them in a way that matches the behavior of the host platform. But that sounds like a pretty tall ask, so personally I'd rather just be able to disable mouse behaviors in opencode entirely to get all my standard platform/terminal behaviors back.

And `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_COPY_ON_SELECT` doesn't solve this because it only disables copying after selecting text — it doesn't change the selection behavior, the scrolling behavior, etc. What we're asking for here is disabling mouse handling _entirely_, so that all standard behaviors like those 1–5 examples work again.
